flowcharts.title: Diagnosis and management of Enterobiasis (pinworm)

nodes.text: Nocturnal perianal itching in a child or household member
Red flag (recurrence despite treatment, genitourinary symptoms, secondary infection)?
Assess for genitourinary involvement and secondary bacterial skin infection
Early-morning perianal cellulose tape test, repeated on consecutive mornings
Eggs seen on the tape test?
Stool microscopy is insensitive; repeat tape testing or consider other causes
Benzimidazole first line: mebendazole or albendazole; pyrantel as alternative
Repeat the dose after about two weeks
Treat household contacts at the same time
Hygiene: handwashing, short nails, no scratching, morning perianal washing
Launder bedding, nightclothes and towels to remove environmental eggs
Benign and readily cured; eradication depends on treating contacts

cells.text: Improves the yield of the tape test
Adult worms, which may occasionally be seen at the anus
Low sensitivity; usually misses the diagnosis
Mebendazole or albendazole; pyrantel pamoate as an alternative
Given after about two weeks, to clear worms maturing from surviving eggs
Simultaneously, to interrupt autoinfection and reinfection

Launder bedding, nightclothes and towels; clean surfaces
Re-treat contacts and reinforce hygiene rather than assuming drug failure
